claims.text: The intervention is to add approximately 0.5 at% yttrium to CoCrFeNi during melting and solidification.
Adding approximately 0.5 at% yttrium will induce in-situ formation of a lubricious oxide phase during sliding.
The yttrium-induced oxide phase will remain stable from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is homogeneous.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has acceptable low-friction performance only at room temperature.
Yttrium will segregate to grain boundaries and sliding interfaces.
Yttrium segregation will promote nucleation and growth of a thin, discontinuous yttrium-rich oxide film during sliding.
The tribofilm may consist of Y2O3 or Y-containing complex oxides.
Yttrium will oxidize preferentially under the proposed tribological conditions.
Preferential yttrium oxidation will produce a stable oxide film with low shear strength.
The yttrium-rich tribo-oxide will act as a solid lubricant and reduce the coefficient of friction as temperature increases.
The yttrium-rich oxide film will reduce wear by protecting the matrix from severe mechanical degradation.
The yttrium-modified alloy will have lower friction coefficients than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The yttrium-modified alloy will have lower wear rates than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi typically develops increased friction and wear at elevated temperatures.
The elevated-temperature friction and wear of unmodified CoCrFeNi arise from uncontrolled oxidation and microstructural degradation.
The predicted benefit is bounded to sliding in air under moderate loads from ambient temperature to 800 °C.
